items.title: Kebbe terror attack: Displaced families battle hunger, trauma
items.description: — Council pays medical bills, distributes relief materials By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto SOKOTO: Families displaced by recent terrorist attacks in Kebbe Local Government Area of Sokoto State are battling hunger, trauma and uncertainty, even as the local government council intensifies efforts to cushion their suffering. The attacks, which reportedly claimed lives and destroyed shops, vehicles and food reserves, forced hundreds of residents of Kebbe, Ungushi, Girkau, Umbutu, Asarara, Nasarawa and other affected communities to flee their homes. Many of the displaced residents are currently taking refuge in communities within Kebbe and neighbouring Jega Local Government Area of Kebbi State, away from their homes and sources of livelihood. In response to the humanitarian crisis, the Kebbe Local Government Council has commenced the distribution of emergency relief materials to affected households while also taking responsibility for the medical treatment of victims wounded during the attacks. The Chairman of Kebbe Local Government Area, Alhaji Musa Garba Kuchi, disclosed that the council had so far distributed 240 bags of 29kg garri, 25 bags of groundnut cake, popularly known as kuli-kuli, and 12 bags of salt to displaced residents. He said the intervention was aimed at addressing the immediate food needs of families who were forced to abandon their communities following the attacks and destruction of their livelihoods. According to him, the council also distributed 200 insecticide-treated mosquito nets, 200 rubber mats, 200 plastic kettles, 200 plastic bowls and other essential household items to the victims. Kuchi said the intervention was not merely a relief gesture but an urgent response to the humanitarian consequences of insecurity. He stressed that the council could not fold its arms while residents who had lost their homes and livelihoods struggled to survive. In a related development, the chairman disclosed that the local government was currently footing the medical bills of 10 victims wounded in the attacks and receiving treatment at the state-owned Orthopaedic Hospital, Wamakko, and other medical facilities. He said the council was paying for all prescribed drugs and other medications required by the patients, adding that the victims were responding positively to treatment. “We are doing everything humanly possible to see to the success of their treatment, including their routine feeding,” Kuchi said. The chairman commended Sokoto State Governor, Ahmed Aliyu Sokoto, for what he described as his swift response to the humanitarian and security challenges confronting communities affected by the attacks. He said the governor’s intervention had provided critical support at a difficult moment. Kuchi, however, stressed that relief materials and medical assistance could only provide temporary succour, insisting that the ultimate solution remained the restoration of security and the safe return of displaced residents to their ancestral communities. Some beneficiaries expressed appreciation to the Kebbe Local Government Council for the intervention but appealed to the government and security agencies to intensify operations against the terrorists and bandits responsible for the attacks. They said they were eager to return home and rebuild their shattered lives. The residents called for sustained security measures to prevent further attacks, protect vulnerable communities and restore normalcy across the affected areas. They stressed that meaningful development could not take place while residents continued to live under the shadow of terror. items.title: Elche - Barcelona en directo | El Barcelona se da un festín ante el Elche en su estreno en la Liga
items.description: El Barcelona se ha dado un festín ante el Elche este domingo en la jornada 2 de la Liga en el Martínez Valero. En el primer acto, Raphinha adelantó a los azulgranas con un tanto de penalti que él mismo provocó. Recibió el brasileño un balón en la frontal, se internó en el área y con un recorte se deshizo de Víctor Chust, que barrió al delantero y cometió penalti. Tras el gol el partido fue decayendo poco a poco, pero justo antes del descanso apareció Adeyemi para anotar el 0-2 y poner tierra de por medio. En el segundo tiempo los azulgrana salieron a controlar la pelota sin arriesgar a perder balones que comprometieran a la defensa con contraataques. Pero los cambios de Flick revolucionaron el choque, especialmente la entrada de Gordon. El inglés repartió en apenas seis minutos sobre el césped dos asistencias. Primero a Raphinha y después a Fermín, que más tarde completaría su doblete para poner el 0-5.

items.title: Drame de Dar-es-Salam : 31 morts et 22 blessés, le CHU Donka mobilisé
items.description: Le bilan de l’éboulement survenu à la décharge de Dar-es-Salam continue de s’alourdir. Selon les autorités sanitaires, la catastrophe a fait 31 morts et 22 blessés. Face à l’ampleur du drame, le dispositif de prise en charge des victimes a été renforcé dans les établissements sanitaires, notamment au CHU Donka. La ministre de la Santé, Dr Khaïté Sall, s’est rendue ce dimanche dans cet établissement afin de s’enquérir de la situation des blessés transférés après l’éboulement. Sur place, la ministre a transmis « le soutien et la compassion du Gouvernement aux familles touchées par cette tragédie ». Elle a également assuré que les victimes bénéficieraient d’une « prise en charge médicale entièrement gratuite ». Les équipes médicales du CHU Donka sont mobilisées pour assurer les soins et le suivi des blessés, en coordination avec les services de secours et la Croix-Rouge. Parmi les 22 blessés recensés, six sont dans un état grave, tandis que 16 présentent des blessures légères. La ministre a salué la mobilisation du personnel du CHU Donka, qui « reste en alerte pour assurer le suivi médical des personnes admises à l’hôpital ». Sur le site de Dar-es-Salam, les opérations de recherche et de secours se poursuivent afin de retrouver d’éventuelles autres victimes. Le ministère de la Santé assure maintenir son dispositif afin de répondre aux besoins médicaux liés à cette catastrophe. Mayi CISSÉ L’article Drame de Dar-es-Salam : 31 morts et 22 blessés, le CHU Donka mobilisé est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: 2027: APC must acknowledge Nigerians’ pains, assure relief — Kawu
items.description: — Senator urges Yari-led campaign council to re-engage grassroots B y Henry Umoru ABUJA: Senator Suleiman Kawu, APC, Kano South, has urged the All Progressives Congress, APC, 2027 Presidential Campaign Council to acknowledge the economic hardships confronting Nigerians and assure citizens of meaningful relief as the party begins its campaign for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election. Kawu, who is the Chairman of the Senate Committee on Downstream Petroleum Sector, made the call in a letter addressed to the Director-General of the campaign council, Senator Abdulaziz Yari, following the release of the 223-member council. In the letter, made available to journalists on Sunday, Kawu urged the campaign council to approach Nigerians with empathy and sensitivity to the socio-economic challenges affecting families across the country. He said the campaign must demonstrate an understanding of the daily struggles of Nigerians and communicate the government’s commitment to providing meaningful relief. The senator also called for renewed engagement with grassroots constituents, warning that a disconnect between political leaders and the electorate could create misconceptions and undermine both the President and the party. According to him, the campaign council must ensure that its activities strictly comply with the Electoral Act and the Constitution to strengthen public confidence in the electoral process. Kawu also urged the council to clearly communicate Tinubu’s policies, programmes and strategic vision to Nigerians, stressing that the President’s achievements and plans must be effectively explained to the electorate. He further called for unity within the APC, urging the campaign council to heal internal divisions, set aside differences and ensure that party leaders and members at all levels were carried along. The senator said victory in the 2027 elections would depend largely on solidarity among members and effective coordination of the party’s structures. He wrote: “I write to extend my warmest congratulations to the Director-General of the Presidential Campaign Council, H.E. Dist. Sen. Abdulaziz Abubakar Yari, and all esteemed members on your well-deserved appointments. Your selection reflects confidence in your experience, leadership and capacity to deliver. “I offer my prayers and best wishes for success as we undertake this critical assignment for our great party, the All Progressives Congress (APC). “As an APC senatorial candidate running on the same ballot and alongside the President, representing the 16 local government areas of Kano South, I recognise the magnitude of the task before us. While we celebrate this appointment, it is imperative that we confront key strategic priorities to ensure total victory.” On addressing the economic realities facing Nigerians, Kawu said: “We must approach our citizens with deep empathy, active listening and genuine sensitivity to the economic hardships and socio-economic challenges currently affecting everyday families. “Our campaign must demonstrate that we truly feel their pain, understand their daily struggles and are sincerely committed to delivering meaningful reliefs.” On grassroots engagement, he said: “A disconnect between leadership and the electorate creates misperceptions and misunderstandings that ultimately undermine both the President and the party.” Kawu also urged the council to uphold electoral integrity, saying: “Our campaign activities must strictly adhere to the provisions of the Electoral Act and the Constitution, ensuring our efforts are rooted in legitimacy and public trust.” On communicating the President’s vision, he said the campaign council must “leverage our collective expertise to clearly convey the President’s key policies, programmes and strategic vision so the public fully recognises his commitment to national progress.” He further stressed the importance of internal cohesion, saying: “Victory depends on complete solidarity. We must heal internal rifts, set aside differences and ensure that all key stakeholders, party leaders and members at every level are fully carried along as equal partners in this mission.” Kawu expressed confidence in Yari’s leadership and capacity to lead the campaign council to victory, while praying for a peaceful and successful electoral process. items.title: Défense : Rafael avance ses pions au Maroc
items.description: Missiles antichars, défense aérienne, missiles air-air à longue portée, missiles de croisière et interception laser : la coopération militaire entre le Maroc et le groupe israélien Rafael couvre désormais un large éventail de capacités. Plusieurs systèmes sont déjà acquis ou sélectionnés, tandis que d’autres font l’objet d’évaluations et de discussions. Le Maroc explore de nouvelles capacités proposées par le groupe israélien Rafael, entre missiles antichars, défense aérienne, frappe à longue portée et interception avancée. Selon le site spécialisé Defense Arabic , cette coopération couvre des systèmes déjà acquis ou sélectionnés, comme Spike et Spyder, mais aussi plusieurs équipements faisant l’objet d’évaluations ou de discussions, notamment Sky Spear, Sky Sonic, Delilah et Iron Beam. Des missiles antichars à la défense aérienne Dans le domaine des missiles antichars, le Maroc a acquis la famille israélienne Spike. La valeur globale du contrat ainsi que l’ensemble des versions commandées n’ont toutefois pas été officiellement dévoilés. Defense Arabic évoque notamment un intérêt ou une utilisation de versions telles que Spike LR2, Spike MR et Spike SR. Ces missiles doivent permettre aux forces terrestres marocaines de disposer de capacités avancées contre les chars et les véhicules blindés. Leur intégration peut concerner aussi bien les unités d’infanterie et les forces spéciales que des plateformes blindées et des tourelles de combat. Sur le volet de la défense aérienne, des sources israéliennes citées par Defense Arabic indiquent que le Maroc a choisi, en mars 2023, le système Spyder de Rafael. Celui-ci repose notamment sur les missiles Python-5 et Derby et est conçu pour faire face à différents types de menaces aériennes, notamment les avions, les drones, les missiles de croisière et les cibles évoluant à basse altitude. Selon le site spécialisé, Spyder devrait s’inscrire dans les différentes couches de la défense aérienne marocaine aux côtés du système Barak MX, déjà entré en service au sein des Forces armées royales. Dans cette configuration, Spyder pourrait assurer l’interception de menaces proches et rapides, tandis que Barak MX couvrirait des distances et des altitudes plus importantes. De nouvelles capacités à l’étude La coopération évoquée par Defense Arabic ne se limite pas aux systèmes déjà acquis ou sélectionnés. Des sources israéliennes indiquent également que le Maroc a évalué les systèmes Sky Spear et Sky Sonic. Le site précise toutefois qu’il n’est pas certain que cet intérêt débouche sur des contrats officiellement annoncés. Une partie de la coopération militaire entre le Maroc et Israël se déroule en effet sans publication détaillée de l’ensemble des informations relatives aux programmes concernés. Sky Sonic fait partie des projets de Rafael destinés à l’interception de menaces balistiques avancées et de missiles hypersoniques. Sky Spear est, pour sa part, présenté comme un missile air-air à longue portée destiné à engager des cibles aériennes à grande distance. L’intérêt évoqué pour ces capacités s’inscrit ainsi dans le prolongement des systèmes déjà concernés par la coopération maroco-israélienne, tout en restant, pour certains programmes, au stade de l’évaluation. Delilah, autre piste étudiée Sur le segment de la frappe à longue portée, Defense Arabic rapporte également des discussions autour du missile de croisière Delilah, qui auraient débuté en juillet 2023. Les discussions porteraient sur des versions aéroportées pouvant être intégrées aux F-16 et aux F-5, ainsi que sur des versions lancées depuis des plateformes terrestres. Le site évoque par ailleurs des estimations faisant état d’un possible achat de plus de 100 missiles, avec l’hypothèse d’une production ou d’un assemblage local au Maroc. La valeur potentielle de cette opération serait estimée entre 300 et 500 millions de dollars, voire davantage. Il est à souligner toutefois que ces chiffres restent des estimations non confirmées, en l’absence d’annonce officielle détaillant les termes d’un éventuel contrat. Le site spécialisé mentionne enfin un intérêt marocain croissant pour Iron Beam, le système laser de Rafael destiné notamment à faire face aux drones et aux menaces aériennes à faible coût. Son principal intérêt réside dans le coût potentiellement inférieur de l’interception par rapport aux missiles conventionnels. items.title: Gamou 2026 : le ministre Alioune Dione veut faire des Dahiras des leviers de création de richesses
items.description: À l’occasion du Gamou 2026, le ministre de la Microfinance et de l’Économie sociale et solidaire, Alioune Dione, veut donner une nouvelle dimension économique aux organisations communautaires de base. S’exprimant, dimanche, à Tivaouane, lors d’un panel organisé par la Commission Entrepreneuriat de la Cellule Zawiya Tidiane, il a appelé à mieux valoriser le capital social, humain et organisationnel des Dahiras pour en faire des espaces d’incubation de PME, de création d’emplois et de production de richesses locales, sans remettre en cause leur vocation spirituelle. Et si les Dahiras devenaient davantage des acteurs du développement économique des territoires ? C’est l’une des pistes avancées, dimanche 23 aout, à Tivaouane, par le ministre de la Microfinance et de l’Économie sociale et solidaire, Alioune Dione. Prenant part à un panel consacré au thème « Comment les organisations communautaires de base peuvent devenir des incubateurs de PME et de richesses locales ? Le cas des Dahiras », il a, d'après la RTS, plaidé pour une meilleure transformation du formidable capital social dont disposent ces organisations en capacité productive. Pour le ministre, les Dahiras ne doivent pas être considérés uniquement comme des espaces de spiritualité, de rassemblement et de solidarité. Ils constituent également des réseaux structurés reposant sur la confiance, les compétences, les ressources et une forte capacité de mobilisation. Autant d’atouts qui, selon lui, peuvent contribuer à la création de valeur, à l’emploi et à l’autonomisation économique des membres des communautés. Le choix de Tivaouane, à l’occasion du Gamou, n’est pas fortuit. Pour Alioune Dione, ce grand rendez-vous religieux offre une illustration concrète de la capacité des communautés à s’organiser et à mutualiser leurs ressources. L’affluence des pèlerins, mais aussi l’activité des commerçants, artisans, transporteurs, femmes et jeunes, traduisent une importante dynamique économique autour de l’événement. « Lorsque la confiance, l’organisation et la solidarité sont réunies, une communauté est capable de produire une formidable énergie collective », a relevé le ministre. L’enjeu consiste désormais à inscrire cette énergie dans la durée. Il ne s’agit toutefois pas, a-t-il précisé, de transformer les Dahiras en entreprises ou de remettre en cause leur vocation religieuse. La démarche vise plutôt à utiliser leur capital social comme un levier supplémentaire d’autonomisation économique. Une évolution résumée par le ministre en une formule : passer « de la solidarité qui accompagne à la solidarité qui autonomise ». Pour concrétiser cette ambition, Alioune Dione a évoqué la mise en place d’un modèle de Coopératives Productives Solidaires (CPS-Dahiras). Le dispositif devrait permettre d’identifier les besoins des membres, mais aussi les opportunités économiques disponibles dans leurs territoires, afin de les organiser autour d’activités génératrices de revenus et d’emplois. Cette orientation s’inscrit dans les actions déjà engagées par le ministère autour de la philanthropie religieuse et de son potentiel pour l’économie sociale et solidaire. Les consultations menées auprès de plusieurs familles religieuses ont notamment permis, selon le ministre, de mesurer l’importance des ressources humaines, financières, organisationnelles et relationnelles disponibles au sein des communautés. Pour accompagner leur transformation en activités économiques durables, plusieurs instruments pourraient être mobilisés. Il s’agit notamment des incubateurs de l’économie sociale et solidaire communaux, des mécanismes d’appui et de financement dédiés à l’ESS et des Boutiques solidaires, destinées à faciliter l’accès aux marchés. Dans cette dynamique, Tivaouane pourrait constituer un premier laboratoire de l’entrepreneuriat communautaire. Le ministre souhaite y procéder à l’identification des filières porteuses, des initiatives existantes, des entrepreneurs et des besoins des communautés, avant de mettre en place les premières CPS-Dahiras. L’expérience devrait ensuite être évaluée afin d’identifier ses forces et ses difficultés et, au besoin, d’ajuster le modèle avant son extension à d’autres foyers religieux du pays. Dans cette perspective, le département de la Microfinance et de l’Économie sociale et solidaire se dit disposé à travailler avec la Cellule Zawiya Tidiane pour la conclusion d’une convention de partenariat. Celle-ci devrait notamment permettre de structurer les CPS-Dahiras, d’accompagner l’incubation des jeunes et des femmes, de faciliter leur accès à des financements adaptés, de renforcer leurs compétences et de favoriser leur digitalisation ainsi que leur accès aux marchés. L’ambition dépasse les frontières nationales. Le ministre a également insisté sur le potentiel que représente la diaspora sénégalaise organisée autour des Dahiras à l’étranger. Il a cité, à titre d’exemple, une expérience menée à Bilbao, en Espagne, avec la Dahira Tidiane locale, qui lui a permis d’échanger sur les possibilités de développer l’économie sociale et solidaire au sein de la diaspora. Pour Alioune Dione, cette approche participe pleinement à la territorialisation du développement. Elle doit permettre de construire une économie moins concentrée dans les grands centres urbains, en donnant aux territoires les moyens de produire, d’entreprendre, de transformer et de créer des emplois. « Une communauté n’est pas seulement un ensemble de personnes qu’il faut accompagner. C’est aussi un ensemble de compétences et de ressources qu’il faut organiser », a-t-il résumé. L’ambition affichée est donc de faire des Dahiras de véritables leviers de production de richesses et de création d’emplois, tout en préservant leur identité et leur vocation spirituelle. Pour le ministre, le défi est désormais de transformer le capital social en capital productif, « sans perdre l’âme et les valeurs qui ont permis de le construire ». Tivaouane pourrait ainsi servir de point de départ à un modèle d’entrepreneuriat communautaire appelé à être expérimenté, évalué puis étendu aux autres foyers religieux du Sénégal.

items.title: Osun: Tinubu’s restraint helped Adeleke win — Imumolen
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA — Former presidential candidate, Prof. Chris Imumolen, has faulted the claim that President Bola Ahmed Tinubu offered no support to Governor Ademola Adeleke’s victory in the August 15 Osun governorship election, arguing that the President’s restraint helped create the conditions for the governor’s re-election. Imumolen said he was not claiming that Tinubu campaigned for Adeleke or funded his campaign. His argument was that the President chose not to deploy the power of his office against an opposition governor, even though the APC had a candidate in the election. In a statement signed by him, Imumolen was reacting to comments by Adeleke’s campaign spokesperson, Pelumi Olajengbesi, who attributed the victory to the will of Osun voters and the governor’s performance in office. “Support in politics is not limited to standing on a campaign platform or openly mobilising votes for a candidate. Sometimes, leadership is demonstrated by what a leader deliberately refuses to do,” Imumolen said. He described Tinubu’s conduct as particularly significant because the APC candidate, Bola Oyebamiji, was contesting against Adeleke. “President Tinubu demonstrated an extraordinary level of democratic restraint in Osun. He remained neutral even when the candidate of his own party was contesting the election,” he said. Imumolen said that restraint allowed political actors, traditional rulers, stakeholders and voters to make their choices without the election becoming a confrontation between the Federal Government and the Osun State Government. “He did not turn the election into a personal battle. He did not deploy the power of his office to intimidate the opposition. Instead, he allowed the people of Osun to make their choice,” he said. He also cited what he described as Tinubu’s intervention concerning the Osun State Government’s account and his reported communication with Adeleke before the result was announced as examples of the President choosing statesmanship over partisan retaliation. “Nobody is saying President Tinubu campaigned for Adeleke. That is not the argument. The point is that the President’s conduct, restraint and democratic disposition contributed to an environment in which Adeleke was able to contest and secure support without the Federal Government turning the election into a presidential power contest,” he said. The President later congratulated Adeleke on his re-election, while the governor visited Tinubu at the Presidential Villa after receiving his Certificate of Return.Imumolen said reducing Tinubu’s role to campaign funding or mobilisation missed the broader political point. “Leadership is not only about what you do for your friends. Sometimes, it is about what you refuse to do to your opponents,” he said. He urged Adeleke and his supporters to acknowledge that restraint rather than dismiss it. “Victory should make a leader magnanimous, not revisionist. The President respected the democratic process in Osun. That fact should not be diminished simply because Adeleke emerged victorious,” Imumolen said. The post Osun: Tinubu’s restraint helped Adeleke win — Imumolen appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Osun guber: Adeleke’s Tinubu backing punctures opposition’s 2027 plan — Presidency
items.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA: The Presidency has said Governor Ademola Adeleke’s decision to support President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid has undermined opposition efforts to use the Osun governorship election as a launching pad for a broader coalition against the All Progressives Congress, APC, ahead of the 2027 general elections. Adeleke’s victory in the August 15 Osun governorship election initially provided the opposition with a new political talking point, the Presidency said. However, his subsequent declaration of support for Tinubu weakened the argument that the election represented a rejection of the President or his administration. Tunde Rahman, Senior Special Assistant to the President on Media and Special Duties, said the Osun outcome was significant for reasons beyond the victory of the Accord Party candidate. He argued that Adeleke’s re-election and his decision to support Tinubu had complicated efforts by opposition politicians to portray the result as evidence of a growing anti-Tinubu movement in the South-West. Adeleke, who contested the election on the Accord Party platform, polled 511,067 votes to defeat the APC candidate, Asiwaju Bola Oyebamiji, popularly known as AMBO, who secured 444,815 votes. Rahman said attempts by opposition forces to portray the victory as a product of a broader political alliance were undermined by Adeleke himself, who, according to him, made it clear that he had no working arrangement with any opposition party or coalition. “Following his victory, an elated Governor Adeleke restated his earlier position to work for President Tinubu’s re-election in 2027. He promised to put everything into the task, including collaborating with the APC members in the state,” he said. The governor subsequently reinforced the position during his August 20 visit to President Tinubu at the Presidential Villa, Abuja, where he presented his certificate of return. During the meeting, Adeleke thanked the President for ensuring a free and fair election, while Tinubu congratulated him on his victory and urged him to embrace unity and reconciliation. The President also advised the governor to broaden his political constituency and refrain from stigmatising his opponents. The Presidency said the development had complicated the opposition’s attempt to turn the Osun result into a launching pad for the 2027 elections. Former Vice President and presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, Alhaji Atiku Abubakar, and other opposition leaders had described the Osun outcome as evidence that Nigerians were seeking an alternative in 2027. However, the Presidency argued that Adeleke’s position did not support such a sweeping interpretation. It said the governor’s declared support for Tinubu, coming shortly after his re-election, demonstrated that the Osun contest should not be reduced to a referendum on the President or the Federal Government. The Presidency also highlighted Tinubu’s decision to congratulate Adeleke before the election results were formally announced as a significant factor in interpreting the outcome. At about 2 a.m. on Sunday, while the results were still being collated, Tinubu reportedly called Adeleke and congratulated him on his victory, telling him that the people of Osun had spoken and given him a mandate to lead the state for another four years. Rahman said the call “changed the political calculus”, portraying Tinubu as “a dyed-in-the-wool democrat, a statesman and a father of all.” He said the President’s action also reinforced the credibility of the electoral process by demonstrating that the Federal Government did not interfere with the outcome. Given the political and institutional influence of the Federal Government, Rahman said Tinubu could have attempted to deploy federal power against Adeleke and his political structure but instead chose to respect the voters’ verdict. The Presidency believes the posture could become politically significant as the 2027 contest intensifies, particularly in the South-West, where the APC has traditionally enjoyed considerable influence. According to the Presidency, the Osun result should also be understood against the backdrop of local political dynamics rather than interpreted as an outright rejection of the APC or Tinubu. Adeleke won 19 of the state’s 30 local government areas, including Ede North, Ede South, Osogbo, Ife Central, Iwo, Ejigbo, Ifelodun, Odo-Otin, Ila and Ayedaade. Oyebamiji won 11 LGAs, including Ilesha East, Ife South, Boripe, Irepodun, Obokun and Olorunda. While Adeleke secured 511,067 votes against Oyebamiji’s 444,815, the APC candidate garnered about 40 per cent of the total votes cast. The 66,252-vote winning margin was also substantially higher than the 28,344-vote difference recorded between Adeleke and former Governor Adegboyega Oyetola in the 2022 election. Rahman said the APC could point to local factors, including internal contradictions within the party and lingering controversies over the policies of previous administrations, as factors that shaped the outcome. The opposition, he noted, would inevitably seek to interpret the election as a rejection of the Federal Government’s economic reforms, particularly policies that initially imposed significant hardship on Nigerians. But he argued that the election was primarily a state contest in which candidates, local issues, party structures and voter preferences played decisive roles. The Presidency believes the immediate implication of the Osun election is that it has effectively accelerated the 2027 political season. Although the presidential campaign formally commenced on August 19, major political blocs are already interpreting the Osun result as an early indicator of voter sentiment. For the opposition, the victory provides a psychological boost and a new political talking point. However, Adeleke’s commitment to Tinubu’s re-election means the opposition cannot easily convert the Accord Party’s victory into a straightforward anti-APC or anti-Tinubu narrative. The Presidency therefore sees the Osun outcome as both a warning and an opportunity for the ruling party: a warning that the South-West remains politically competitive and an opportunity to strengthen engagement with voters ahead of 2027. With months to the presidential election, the political contest has effectively begun. And while the opposition may have secured an important headline from Osun, the Presidency believes Adeleke’s decision to back Tinubu has denied it the broader political dividend it hoped to derive from the governor’s victory. The post Osun guber: Adeleke’s Tinubu backing punctures opposition’s 2027 plan — Presidency appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Onitsha traders demand removal of Ogbogwu market caretaker committee
items.description: — Seek election of market executive after police shooting By Nwabueze Okonkwo ONITSHA: Aggrieved traders at the popular Ogbogwu Drug Market in Onitsha, Anambra State, have renewed calls for the removal of the market’s caretaker committee chairman, Mr Ndubuisi Chukwuleta, and the conduct of an election to usher in a democratically elected executive. The demand followed last Wednesday’s shooting incident involving some traders and policemen at the Onitsha Bridgehead, where several persons were reportedly injured. The incident occurred when some armed policemen in mufti allegedly opened fire on traders they suspected were carrying a bag containing unregistered drugs purchased from the Ogbogwu market. The shooting reportedly sparked tension among traders and passers-by and nearly degenerated into a protest before the intervention of the Anambra State Commissioner of Police, CP Nnanna Oji Ama. Ama, who visited the scene and the hospitals where some of the injured victims were receiving treatment, ordered a comprehensive and impartial investigation into the circumstances surrounding the incident. He also reportedly promised to settle the medical bills of the victims. The commissioner expressed disappointment with some police Area Commanders and Divisional Police Officers over their alleged failure to properly control their subordinates and ensure compliance with police rules of engagement. At White Chapel Hospital, Fegge, Onitsha, where two of the injured persons were receiving treatment, one of the victims, Mr Obiora Nweke, said he was not the person carrying the bag of drugs allegedly being sought by the policemen. Nweke, a native of Anaku in Ayamelum Local Government Area of the state, said he worked as a loader around the Ogbogwu market. According to him, he was loading a vehicle when he heard a commotion around the Bridgehead end of the Enugu-Onitsha Expressway and went to find out what was happening. He said he saw a man inside a drainage channel arguing with some persons, whom he did not initially know were policemen in mufti. Nweke said one of the policemen suddenly pulled out a firearm and shot him in the leg. He said he initially thought the gunshot had been fired into the ground but later realised he had been hit after severe pain set in, causing him to collapse. Nweke said he regained consciousness at the hospital, where he saw the police commissioner at his bedside. He explained that the commissioner authorised the hospital to commence full treatment after the facility had initially provided first aid and requested police authorisation before treating him for a gunshot injury. Another victim, Prince Friday Osisi, who sustained an injury to his forehead and underwent surgery, said he was hit by a stone allegedly thrown at the policemen by angry traders shortly after the shooting. Osisi, a trader at Ogbogwu market and Public Relations Officer of Virtues for Ogbogwu Market Traders Association, said he had alerted the state Police Public Relations Officer, SP Tochukwu Ikenga, about the incident. He said by the time the police commissioner, Ikenga, the Onitsha Area Commander and other senior officers arrived at the hospital, he was already undergoing surgery. Osisi alleged that the caretaker committee chairman had failed to adequately protect the interests of traders in the market. He called on the state government to dissolve the caretaker arrangement and conduct an election to usher in an elected market leadership. “From my own last count, no fewer than seven persons were shot by those policemen on mufti, and the victims are currently lying in various hospitals,” he said. “Our caretaker committee chairman, Chukwuleta, who has incidentally spent over four years in office, is not protecting the interests of the traders but working against them. “I am therefore calling on the state government to remove Chukwuleta from office, dissolve the caretaker system in Ogbogwu market and conduct an election that will usher in an elected leadership.” Also speaking, the leader of Virtues for Ogbogwu Market Traders Association, Chibeze Ifejiofor, who visited Osisi at the hospital, called on Governor Chukwuma Soludo and the Commissioner for Industry, Trade and Investment, Mr Nonso Ebonwu, to remove Chukwuleta and organise an election. Ifejiofor, also known as Chibeze Adamu, alleged that traders had experienced several challenges under the caretaker arrangement. “We traders at Ogbogwu market have suffered a lot of problems with Chukwuleta. Last year, it was NAFDAC that came and closed the market for upward of two months and looted many shops, claiming that they found unregistered drugs,” he alleged. He appealed to the government to conduct the long-awaited election, saying traders had resolved since last year to elect a substantive executive. According to him, the traders were asked to wait until after the November 2025 governorship election in the state. He said the election had since been concluded, but the market leadership poll had yet to take place. “We want government to conduct it as soon as possible, preferably by September or October this year,” he said. Meanwhile, one of the medical experts at White Chapel Hospital, Dr Celestine Orji, said the conditions of the two injured victims had stabilised. He added that there was no fracture of the bone or extraction of pellets from Nweke’s leg. The hospital’s administrative officer, Mrs Ezechukwu, said the medical bills of the two patients had been prepared and issued to them for onward submission to the police commissioner, who had promised to assist with the expenses. When contacted, Chukwuleta declined to comment on the allegations, saying the incident had nothing to do with Ogbogwu market or its bona fide members because it occurred outside the market. items.title: Tinubu to chair AMSG roundtable on critical minerals development in Africa
items.description: — As AMSG pushes for resource wealth, mineral value addition B y Gabriel Ewepu ABUJA: The Africa Minerals Strategy Group, AMSG, has disclosed that President Bola Tinubu will chair its third High-Level Roundtable on Critical Minerals Development in Africa in Manhattan, New York, United States, on September 21, 2026. The roundtable, themed “From Resources to Wealth: Continental Cooperation for Mineral Value Addition,” is aimed at promoting resource wealth and mineral value addition in Africa. The gathering underscores Africa’s determination to place critical minerals at the centre of the continent’s industrial, economic and geopolitical agenda. According to AMSG, the high-level meeting will bring together African heads of state and government representatives, ministers, global investors, development finance institutions, multilateral organisations and executives from the mining, technology, processing, logistics and mineral traceability industries. The group said the roundtable comes at a pivotal moment in the global race for critical minerals, as lithium, copper, cobalt, graphite, manganese, rare earth elements and other strategic resources become increasingly important to technologies, energy systems, defence industries and manufacturing supply chains shaping the global economy. Africa possesses some of the world’s most significant reserves of many of these minerals. However, for decades, much of the continent’s mineral wealth has left African shores with limited processing and value addition taking place locally. Rather than serving as another forum for declarations, AMSG said the roundtable would focus on bankable opportunities, policy alignment, investment structures and mechanisms capable of converting Africa’s mineral endowment into measurable economic value. The organisation said the September gathering represents an important test of Africa’s ability to act collectively at a time when critical minerals are becoming increasingly central to global economic and national security strategies. AMSG said Africa must move from being a passive participant in global mineral supply chains to becoming an active architect of the emerging mineral economy. The New York gathering will feature ministerial representatives from AMSG member states, multilateral institutions, development finance institutions, including the Africa Finance Corporation, as well as invited executives from major global mining, technology, traceability and logistics companies. Their participation is expected to create a convergence between African policymakers overseeing mineral resources, institutions capable of financing large-scale development and private-sector players seeking secure and sustainable critical-mineral supply chains. The Third AMSG High-Level Roundtable is strategically partnered and supported by Core International. Established in January 2024 by African governments as a continental intergovernmental organisation and specialised agency for critical minerals development, AMSG serves as a platform for coordinating critical-minerals policy, investment alignment, minerals security and Africa’s engagement with global partners. AMSG said the traditional extract-and-export model must change, adding that the New York roundtable would focus on how African countries could build integrated mineral value chains, attract transformative capital, strengthen continental cooperation and secure a greater share of the economic value generated from the continent’s mineral resources. The roundtable represents a major step in the implementation of the Mutual Assured Development, MADE, Framework, launched at the African Natural Resources and Energy Investment Summit, AFNIS 2026, in Abuja. Building on the framework, the New York gathering will mark what AMSG described as a transition from strategic dialogue to structural execution, with the official unveiling of the Continental Integration and Economic Assurance Declaration, CIEAD. The declaration is expected to provide a new continental architecture for cooperation around critical minerals, including policy coordination, investment mobilisation, mineral value addition, supply-chain security and mechanisms for strengthening Africa’s negotiating position in the global minerals economy. According to the group, a key component will be the proposed CIEAD Finance Window, designed to support innovative financing structures capable of mobilising capital for mineral processing, infrastructure, technology and other critical components of Africa’s emerging mineral value chains. The roundtable will be convened by the leadership of AMSG, with the participation of the Minister of Solid Minerals Development and Chairperson of the AMSG Ministerial Steering Committee, Mr Dele Alake, and the Secretary-General of AMSG, Mr Moses Micheal Engadu. The stakes for Africa, AMSG said, extend well beyond mining. The global transition to electric mobility, renewable energy, advanced manufacturing, artificial intelligence, digital infrastructure and modern defence systems is intensifying competition for secure supplies of critical minerals. The development has placed Africa at the centre of a rapidly changing global economic and geopolitical landscape. AMSG said the continent now has an opportunity to leverage its mineral endowment to drive manufacturing, technology transfer, infrastructure development, regional trade and job creation rather than remain primarily a source of raw materials for industries elsewhere. “The Roundtable will therefore examine practical pathways for African countries to develop integrated and competitive mineral value chains, strengthen intra-African cooperation and attract long-term investment into processing, refining, manufacturing and related infrastructure,” the group added. items.title: Two security operatives reportedly killed in fresh Plateau attack
items.description: By Golok Nanmwa, Jos JOS: At least two security operatives have reportedly been killed, while several others were injured during a renewed attack on communities in Jol District of Riyom Local Government Area of Plateau State. The attackers also reportedly carted away the firearms of the slain security personnel. The incident occurred on Sunday afternoon when suspected armed attackers stormed Tanjol and Tarai communities in the area and opened fire on residents. Sources in the community said the attackers invaded the two communities at about 2:30 p.m., prompting security personnel in the area to respond. The operatives reportedly encountered fierce resistance from the attackers, resulting in a gun battle that lasted several minutes. Sources from the local government said information available indicated that at least two security operatives were killed during the encounter, while their firearms were reportedly taken away by the attackers. Some residents were also reportedly injured in the attack, while one civilian was said to be missing. A resident of the area, Mr Jerry Chollom, who confirmed the development, said the incident had created fear and tension among residents, particularly those in communities around Jol. Chollom said residents were worried about the safety of their lives and property, urging security agencies to intensify efforts to protect vulnerable communities in the area. Efforts to obtain reactions from the security agencies were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report. The post Two security operatives reportedly killed in fresh Plateau attack appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: I don’t hate Christians — Sheikh Jingir
items.description: — Urges Tinubu, governors to ensure justice, fairness for all Nigerians By Golok Nanmwa JOS: Chairman of the Izalatil Bid’a Wa’ikamatis Sunnah, JIBWIS, Sheikh Sani Yahaya Jingir, has dismissed claims that he dislikes Christians, describing the allegations as “mere lies” and a misinterpretation of his recent remarks. The Islamic cleric came under criticism following comments he made at a mass wedding ceremony organised by the Kano State Government for 1,500 couples, which some Nigerians described as divisive along religious lines. However, speaking on Sunday at a one-day national symposium with the theme, “Enhanced Political Participation and Social Justice as a Panacea for Unity and Development in Nigeria,” held in Jos, Jingir said his remarks were not intended to express hatred towards Christians or non-Muslims. He said: “A lot of people are saying I dislike Christians. I didn’t say I dislike Christians. It is a lie. My remarks were misinterpreted. “Leadership in Islam is not about cheating people of different faiths. Islam teaches us to share love with people of different faiths or sects.” Jingir further explained that Islam teaches fairness and justice to people irrespective of their religious affiliation, stressing that Muslims would be accountable for any injustice committed against non-Muslims. He added that Prophet Muhammad (SAW) lived peacefully with people of other faiths and urged Nigerians to promote peaceful coexistence. The cleric also called on President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, governors and other political leaders to ensure fairness and justice in the discharge of their responsibilities, irrespective of the ethnic, religious or political affiliations of the people they govern. “I call on President Bola Ahmed Tinubu not to cheat non-Muslims and Muslims alike. I also call on you not to cheat those who are not in the same political party with you. “You should lead with justice and fairness to all Nigerians,” he said. Jingir maintained that every Nigerian had the right to freely choose and support any candidate of his or her choice during elections. “Everyone has the right to vote for whoever he feels is okay with him to vote for during an election,” he said. The JIBWIS chairman urged Nigerians to embrace peace, unity and togetherness, stressing that sustainable development could not be achieved in an atmosphere of insecurity and division. “Without peace, there will be no development,” he said, calling on Nigerians to work towards strengthening peaceful coexistence among the various ethnic and religious groups in the country. The post I don’t hate Christians — Sheikh Jingir appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Atiku’s subsidy proposal’ll wreck Nigeria’s recovery — Rep Ahmed
items.description: By Dapo Akinrefon LAGOS: The lawmaker representing Agege Federal Constituency, Dr Wale Ahmed, has faulted former Vice President Atiku Abubakar’s proposal to restore petrol subsidy, warning that the policy could derail Nigeria’s economic recovery. Ahmed, in a statement, described the proposal by the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, as economically unsustainable and politically expedient. Atiku had promised to restore petrol subsidy if elected president in 2027, arguing that Nigerians had suffered significantly since President Bola Tinubu removed the subsidy. But Ahmed said reversing the policy would return Nigeria to an expensive system that drained public resources and created opportunities for abuse. The lawmaker said: “Nigeria cannot afford to return to the subsidy era. What we need is to consolidate reforms and ensure their benefits reach ordinary Nigerians.” He said the removal of subsidy had improved government revenues by freeing up resources previously committed to keeping petrol prices artificially low. “The question should be how these additional resources are deployed to improve infrastructure, healthcare, education, transportation and security, not how we recreate an unsustainable subsidy regime,” he said. Challenging Atiku to explain how his proposed subsidy arrangement would be funded without worsening Nigeria’s fiscal position, Ahmed said: “Where will the money come from? Will government borrow again to finance subsidy? Will allocations to states and local governments be reduced? Nigerians deserve clear answers.” The lawmaker said the claim that subsidy savings had disappeared was misleading, noting that the resources accrued to the federation. He said: “The savings were not money kept in a vault by the Federal Government. They increased revenues available to the federation and were shared among the three tiers of government. “Nobody is denying the hardship. It is real. But returning to the policies that contributed to our fiscal problems cannot be the solution.” He urged the Federal Government to accelerate measures to reduce production and transportation costs, including improvements in electricity supply and investment in agriculture. Expressing confidence in Tinubu’s chances of securing another term in 2027, Ahmed said: “I strongly support President Tinubu for 2027. Nigerians will ultimately choose sustainable economic management over promises that may offer temporary relief but create deeper problems.” The post Atiku’s subsidy proposal’ll wreck Nigeria’s recovery — Rep Ahmed appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Police uncover adulterated drinks warehouse in Warri
items.description: The Police Command in Delta says it has uncovered a warehouse in Warri used for adulterated beverages. The command spokesman, SP Bright Edafe, said this in a statement on Sunday in Warri. Edafe said the State Anti-Kidnapping Unit (SAKU) of the command discovered the warehouse on Monday. He said the police team was conducting a stop-and-search operation on the Warri–Agbarho Expressway when they intercepted a Toyota Sienna carrying quantities of the beverage. “The operatives intercepted a Toyota Sienna conveying quantities of “Gbefun hot drink” suspected to be adulterated and arrested the 44-year-old driver. “Further investigation led the operatives to a warehouse at Lower Neighborhood in Ginuwa, Warri, where additional quantities of the suspected adulterated drink were recovered. “Another beverage and a Suzuki Shuttle bus, loaded with similar products, were also recovered at the premises of the warehouse,” he said. Edafe said that the suspected operators of the warehouse fled on sighting the police. The police spokesman added that efforts were on top gear to arrest the fleeing suspects and unravel the source and distribution network. He said that the Commissioner of Police in charge of the command, Mr Yemi Oyeniyi, commended the operatives for their professionalism. items.title: Hamzat, Oshiomhole, Shekarau push stronger national identity
items.description: — Urge Nigerians to shun ethnicity, religious bigotry By Olasunkanmi Akoni Lagos State Deputy Governor, Dr. Kadri Obafemi Hamzat, has stressed the need for Nigerians to make deliberate efforts to build a stronger national identity that transcends ethnic, religious and cultural differences. Senator representing Edo North, Comrade Adams Oshiomhole, and former Kano State Governor, Mallam Ibrahim Shekarau, also supported the call, urging Nigerians to shun ethnic and religious biases. Speaking at the 7th National Discourse, themed, “Interrogating Nigeria’s Democracy in the Context of Multiple Diversity,” held at the J.F. Ade Ajayi Auditorium, University of Lagos, UNILAG, Akoka, Lagos, on Sunday, Hamzat said Nigeria’s political system must find effective ways to accommodate its diverse identities without allowing them to undermine national unity. According to him, ethnic and religious identities remain deeply rooted in the country’s social and political life, adding that the challenge was not to eliminate such identities but to prevent them from becoming instruments of division. “The question that sociologists have not told us is how we marry our culture and democracy, without losing our identity and putting it into our democratic setting. And I think that will be the issue for us. “As Nigerians, we must learn to accommodate our differences while we are also promoting a common national identity. The experience of other multi-ethnic societies showed the dangers of allowing identity and class differences to fuel conflict among us,” the deputy governor said. He advocated greater religious tolerance and adherence to the core teachings of Islam and Christianity, urging citizens to respect the faith of others rather than use religion as a basis for discrimination. Hamzat also stressed the importance of culture in strengthening national unity and urged Nigerians to preserve their cultural heritage while building a common national identity. Oshiomhole, in his contribution, called on Nigerians to shun ethnic and religious divisions and build a nation where leadership is determined by competence, ideas and values rather than place of birth or religious affiliation. He added that ethnicity and religion should not be used as tools for political mobilisation or to shield leaders from accountability. The senator said Nigeria’s diversity should be regarded as an asset capable of driving national development rather than a source of division, noting that a society where citizens are treated fairly irrespective of ethnicity, religion or place of birth would experience greater development. “Our ethnicity shouldn’t be a source of challenge. It should give us all of the things that we need to be the greatest country, not only in Africa but in the world. “This ethnicity is very dysfunctional. Nobody should be rewarded or punished on account of an accident of birth. Ethnicity has very little or no role to play, except to function as a tool in the hands of a segment of the political elite who substitute ethnicity in place of ideas,” Oshiomhole said. While urging political leaders and citizens to embrace a broader sense of Nigerian identity, the senator said the country’s abundant human and natural resources could make it one of the greatest nations in Africa and the world if properly harnessed. In his remarks, Chairman of the occasion, Shekarau, called for greater religious tolerance and understanding among Nigerians, saying there was no justification for religious conflict in a country where citizens, regardless of their faith, are all creations of Allah. Shekarau urged Nigerians to deepen their understanding of the teachings of their respective religions, noting that all faiths promote values such as love, kindness, justice and respect for others. He stressed that if Nigerians genuinely practised the teachings of their religions, the country would be a better place to live, adding that religious differences should not be allowed to fuel conflict or division. Identifying consultation, fairness and respect for divergent views as essential principles of politics and good governance, the former governor cautioned political leaders against pursuing personal interests at the expense of the people. Earlier, the National Amir of The Companion, Imam Noreem Jimoh, said the event was convened to critically examine the challenges confronting Nigeria’s democracy within the context of its diversity. He urged Nigerians to interrogate the country’s democratic journey and seek practical ways to make it work more effectively, particularly in managing the nation’s ethnic, religious, cultural and regional diversities. Jimoh added that Nigeria’s enormous ethnic, linguistic, religious, cultural, regional, economic and social diversity remained both a source of strength and a major challenge to nation-building. He noted that while the country’s diversity gives it significant potential, its effective management remains critical to the success of its democracy. He stressed that the ability of the democratic system to accommodate and harness those differences was one of the key issues the event sought to address. In his lecture, themed “Nigeria’s Political Landscape and the Ethno-Religious Divides: Interrogating Nigeria’s Democracy in the Context of Multi-Diversity,” former Director-General of the Administrative Staff College of Nigeria, ASCON, Prof. Liasu Jinadu, identified ethnicity as a major factor that has shaped Nigeria’s political development since the colonial era, particularly through the country’s ethno-regional political structure and multi-party system. According to him, political elites have exploited ethnic identities to establish patron-client relationships and secure political support, thereby weakening state institutions and undermining the autonomy of government. He maintained that ethnicity had consequently been used to mask issues of political impunity, corruption, patronage and abuse of political power. Jinadu charged that citizens must be empowered to participate meaningfully in governance, irrespective of their ethnic or religious identities. He maintained that the denial of economic and social opportunities, transparency, protective security and other basic freedoms prevents citizens from fully exercising their rights. He therefore called for a political system that places citizenship, human security and human development above ethnic interests, in line with the principles of Nigeria’s 1999 Constitution. The post Hamzat, Oshiomhole, Shekarau push stronger national identity appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: ‎Tansila : Un enfant perd la vie après avoir reçu un coup de bâton destiné à sa mère
items.description: ‎Un enfant est décédé le vendredi 21 août 2026 à Orowé, village situé à 10 km de la commune de Tansila. Selon l'agence d'information du Burkina qui rapporte l'information, il aurait été atteint par un coup de bâton porté par son père contre sa mère lors d'une dispute conjugale. ‎Selon les informations recueillies par l'AIB, l'incident est survenu à la suite d'une dispute entre un homme et son épouse. Emporté par la colère, l'homme aurait tenté de frapper sa femme à l'aide d'un bâton. Pour éviter le coup, celle-ci aurait esquivé le bâton qui a malheureusement atteint l'enfant qui se trouvait à proximité. ‎Grièvement touché, l'enfant a été rapidement conduit au Centre de santé et de promotion sociale (CSPS) de la localité. Il a malheureusement succombé à ses blessures quelques instants après son admission. ‎ ‎Lefaso.net ‎Source : AIB

items.title: Assainissement : le projet des dix villes relancé à Kaolack
items.description: À deux jours du Gamou international de Médina Baye, le ministre de l’Hydraulique et de l’Assainissement, Cheikh Tidiane Dièye, a annoncé, dimanche 23 aout, la relance effective du projet d’assainissement des dix villes du Sénégal, dont Kaolack. Après une période d’arrêt, le programme doit permettre de renforcer durablement les capacités d’évacuation des eaux pluviales dans la capitale du Saloum, confrontée à des difficultés récurrentes d’assainissement en période d’hivernage. Le projet d’assainissement des dix villes du Sénégal connaît un nouveau départ. En déplacement à Kaolack, dimanche, le ministre de l’Hydraulique et de l’Assainissement, Cheikh Tidiane Dièye, a annoncé le redémarrage effectif des travaux, après une période d’arrêt marquée par la nécessité de réévaluer le programme et de mobiliser les ressources nécessaires à sa poursuite. « Le plus important aujourd’hui, c’est le redémarrage effectif de ce grand projet des dix villes du Sénégal, dont Kaolack », a déclaré le ministre à l’issue d’une visite d’évaluation du dispositif de gestion des eaux pluviales mis en place dans la ville en perspective du Gamou international de Médina Baye. Selon lui, le programme avait enregistré des avancées importantes avant de connaître un arrêt. Depuis l’arrivée de la nouvelle équipe gouvernementale, des évaluations ont été menées afin d’identifier les travaux à reprendre et les moyens nécessaires à leur accélération. « À notre arrivée, entre 2024 et 2025, nous avions fait toutes les visites pour regarder ce qu’il fallait reprendre et accélérer. Après, il fallait remobiliser et trouver des marges financières et budgétaires », a-t-il expliqué. Malgré les contraintes budgétaires, l’État est parvenu à mobiliser les ressources nécessaires pour permettre la reprise des travaux. L’entreprise chargée de leur exécution a été remobilisée et doit désormais poursuivre les interventions en vue de finaliser les ouvrages prévus à Kaolack. Parmi les infrastructures concernées figure le bassin de Thiofack, visité par le ministre. Cet ouvrage joue un rôle important dans la collecte et l’évacuation des eaux pluviales provenant des quartiers environnants. Pour Cheikh Tidiane Dièye, la relance de ce projet doit permettre à Kaolack de disposer d’un système d’assainissement plus durable et mieux adapté aux besoins de la ville. La capitale du Saloum, de par sa position géographique, son poids démographique et l’importance de l’affluence enregistrée chaque année à l’occasion du Mawlid de Médina Baye, nécessite, selon lui, des investissements conséquents dans le domaine de l’assainissement. « Kaolack mérite d’être assainie », a-t-il notamment souligné, estimant que la ville doit être accompagnée par un programme moderne et ambitieux. Un dispositif hivernal jugé satisfaisant Le ministre a, par ailleurs, dressé un bilan positif du dispositif mis en place à Kaolack pour faire face aux eaux pluviales. Une première visite effectuée environ deux mois auparavant avait permis d’évaluer les ouvrages et équipements installés en prélude à l’hivernage, notamment les opérations de curage et les différents dispositifs de drainage. Ces interventions ont été menées avec la Direction de la prévention et de la gestion des inondations, le Génie militaire, la Brigade nationale des sapeurs-pompiers et l’Office national de l’assainissement du Sénégal (ONAS). Selon le ministre, ces actions ont contribué à améliorer l’évacuation des eaux dans plusieurs zones de la ville. Des difficultés persistent néanmoins dans certains secteurs, notamment à Thiofack, où des « points endémiques » caractérisés par des eaux stagnantes ont été relevés. À l’approche du Gamou de Médina Baye, Cheikh Tidiane Dièye a appelé les populations à préserver les ouvrages réalisés et à éviter d’y déverser des déchets solides. « Il faut éviter de remettre des déchets dans les canaux qui sont déjà curés parce que c’est cela qui nous crée des difficultés », a-t-il insisté.

items.title: Atiku mourns Ogogo, says actor’s death leaves ‘painful void’ in Nollywood
items.description: Former Vice-President and presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress, Atiku Abubakar, has mourned veteran Nollywood actor Taiwo Hassan, popularly known as Ogogo, who died on Sunday at the age of 66. Atiku, in a statement posted on X, described the actor’s death as “deeply saddening,” noting that it came only days after the public became aware of his battle with cancer. “The news of the passing of celebrated Nollywood actor, Alhaji Taiwo Hassan, is deeply saddening,” Atiku said. He described Hassan as more than an accomplished actor, saying his career had left a lasting impact on Nigeria’s entertainment industry and society. “Through a remarkable career, he brought laughter into countless homes, told stories that reflected our society and used his talent not only to entertain but also to educate and inspire social rebirth,” the former vice-president said. Atiku said the actor’s death had created a significant void in Nigeria’s creative sector and among his numerous admirers. “His passing leaves a painful void in Nigeria’s creative community and in the hearts of the millions who cherished his work,” he said. The ADC presidential candidate expressed condolences to Hassan’s family, colleagues and admirers in Nigeria and abroad, praying for divine comfort for those mourning him. “I join his family, colleagues and admirers in Nigeria and across the world in mourning this profound loss,” Atiku said. He prayed that Allah would forgive the late actor’s shortcomings, comfort his loved ones and grant him eternal rest. “May Almighty Allah forgive his shortcomings, comfort his loved ones and grant him eternal rest in Al-Jannah Firdaus,” he added. Hassan, widely recognised as one of the prominent figures in Yoruba-language Nollywood, died on Sunday at 66 after a battle with cancer. His death came shortly after his daughters, Kira and Haleemah, disclosed that the actor had been battling stage-four cancer and appealed for support as the family sought treatment options. items.title: Jide Kosoko, others pay tribute to late Taiwo ‘Ogogo’ Hassan
items.description: Colleagues of veteran Yoruba actor, Taiwo Hassan, popularly known as Ogogo, have expressed grief over his death. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that Hassan’s family confirmed his passing on Sunday at the age of 66. Hassan, who rose to prominence in the 1990s, was celebrated for his roles in Yoruba action and epic films such as Ogogo, Eegun Mogaji and Igbekun. He was known for his commanding screen presence and dedication to promoting Yoruba culture through cinema. Renowned actor, Jide Kosoko, mourned ‘Ogogo’, noting that the late thespian left an indelible mark on Yoruba cinema. Actor and President of the Theatre Arts and Motion Pictures Practitioners Association of Nigeria (TAMPAN), Bolaji Amusan, popularly known as Mr Latin, also paid tribute to Ogogo. In a statement, he said: “Today, we mourn the passing of a great icon, a legend and a father to many. “Taiwo Ogogo Hassan lived a remarkable life, touched countless hearts and left an indelible mark on our industry and culture. May his legacy live on forever, and may God grant his family, colleagues and loved ones the strength to bear this painful loss.” Actor Saidi Balogun expressed grief over the passing of Ogogo, describing him as a brother. In an emotional tribute shared online, Balogun wrote: “You can rest now, my brother, Taiwo Hassan Ogogo. May Almighty Allah guide you through Aljannah. This is truly painful.” Balogun said Ogogo was not just a colleague but family, and prayed that Allah grants him eternal rest. Similarly, actor Femi Adebayo described Ogogo as a true pillar of Yoruba cinema whose impact would live on for generations. “Thank you for the years, the stories, the lessons and the moments that made us fall in love with the craft,” Adebayo said. Actress Toyin Adewale described Hassan as a “gem”, saying his life and legacy were remarkable. “We lost a gem. Sir T, you came, you saw, and you conquered. What a remarkable life and legacy,” Adewale said. She prayed for the veteran actor to rest peacefully, adding that his memories would remain in the hearts of those who knew him. The post Jide Kosoko, others pay tribute to late Taiwo ‘Ogogo’ Hassan appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Atiku politicizing nation’s economy with his flip-flops on subsidy – Presidency
items.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA — The Presidency has accused former Vice President Atiku Abubakar of politicising Nigeria’s economy after he renewed calls to restore the petrol subsidy, saying the stance sharply contradicts the economic position he took during the 2023 presidential campaign. The Presidency described Atiku’s recent stance as political opportunism that seeks to capitalize on Nigerians’ economic hardships for electoral gain, instead of proposing a viable alternative to the government’s current reform programme. Sunday Dare, the President’s Special Adviser on Media and Public Communications, said in a statement that Atiku had earlier called for the removal of the petrol subsidy, describing the regime as unsustainable, opaque and prone to corruption. Titled: “Atiku’s Subsidy U-Turn: The Bankruptcy of Desperate Ambition, ” Dare said: “In the architecture of modern political opportunism, few spectacles rival the breathtaking hypocrisy of Alhaji Atiku Abubakar’s recent policy pivot. “To watch a self-styled statesman—who less than four years ago cast himself as an uncompromising apostle of market-driven reform—scramble to promise the reintroduction of petrol subsidies is nothing short of political apostasy. “This isn’t merely a tactical policy disagreement; it is a sordid, stingy manipulation of the public psyche, designed to hoodwink unsuspecting citizens through an unpardonable exploitation of temporary economic pain. “Atiku’s vacillation stands as a monument to a fading presidential ambition gone completely awry, exposing a man willing to burn down national economic stability for a fleeting headline.” On what he described as a chronicle of political duplicity, he said: “Let us refresh the collective memory of the Nigerian electorate, which Atiku so cynically presumes to be short. During the intense build-up to the 2023 general election, Atiku made the total removal of the fuel subsidy the absolute cornerstone of his economic manifesto. “He argued with unyielding conviction—repeatedly echoed across national media platforms, including broad coverage by outlets like Premium Times and The Punch—that the opaque, corruption-ridden import subsidy regime was bleeding the nation dry, enriching a parasitic cabal, and mortgaging the future of generations unborn. “Yet, as the political calendar ticks toward the next electoral cycle and the reality of his diminished prospects sets in, Atiku has engineered a shameless volte-face. The architect of yesterday’s fiscal discipline has overnight transformed into the high priest of populist pandering. “This radical reversal is the ultimate hallmark of a desperate politician who cares less about long-term fiscal sustainability and more about capturing power by any means necessary. It is a cynical bet that Nigerians have forgotten his own economic doctrine—a scorched-earth strategy that weaponizes current hardships against the very structural reforms he once championed.” He described the position of the former vice president as “the desperation of a fading ambition.” According to him: “Atiku’s career has long been shadowed by the relentless pursuit of the elusive presidency, an ambition that has increasingly degenerated into a reflex of contrarian posturing. When an administration undertakes the tortuous, necessary surgery of dismantling an unsustainable subsidy regime—a framework legally sealed by the Petroleum Industry Act—it inevitably invites short-term adjustment pains. “Rather than offering statesmanlike support or constructive alternatives, Atiku has chosen the path of political opportunism. His visible annoyance at the ongoing recovery across various sectors of our national life is telling. “The emergence of domestic refining capacity, the liberation of trillions of naira into the Federation Account for sub-national infrastructural development, and the steady weaning of the Nigerian economy from life-support leakages are milestones that threaten his political narrative. By promising to roll back these hard-won gains, Atiku reveals a transactional worldview: if he cannot rule, he would rather preside over ruins.” On what he termed as “a sordid rebuttal to economic regression*, the presidency said: “To entertain Atiku’s hollow promise is to invite national economic suicide. The old import subsidy regime was not merely a pricing mechanism; it was a black hole of rent-seeking, round-tripping, and monumental corruption that starved health, education, and infrastructure of vital capital. “Restoring it would instantly sabotage the nascent renaissance of local refining, crush private sector confidence, and plunge the country back into chronic foreign exchange haemorrhage. Nigerians must reject this sordid narrative of regression. “True leadership requires the courage to defend difficult, foundational reforms even when the political weather is rough, rather than pandering to populist illusions for ballot-box validation. “Atiku’s hypocrisy is an insult to the collective intelligence of a resilient populace navigating global economic headwinds. By the Grace of God, this desperate gambit will fail, and all citizens of conscience must rise up to soundly repudiate this political innuendo.” The post Atiku politicizing nation’s economy with his flip-flops on subsidy – Presidency appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Weah calls for independent judiciary to safeguard democracy
items.description: — As Fubara charges judges to consider effect of judgments on nation’s polity By Daniel Abia, P/Harcourt With barely six months to the 2027 presidential election, former Liberian President George Opong Weah has urged legal practitioners to remain neutral in the administration of justice, describing an independent judiciary as crucial to safeguarding democracy. Weah, who delivered a keynote address at the 66th Annual General Conference of the Nigerian Bar Association, NBA, in Port Harcourt, Rivers State, emphasised the crucial role of the Bar and Bench in safeguarding the rights and freedoms of citizens. He noted that an independent judiciary, protected by a fearless legal profession, “is needed in every serious nation”, warning that threats to democracy do not come only from the barrel of a gun or a defeated leader who refuses to hand over power. He said democracy could also be threatened when judicial institutions are weakened and unable to perform their duties effectively. The former Liberian leader reminded delegates that democracy does not end on election night but is tested every day, stressing that “democracy cannot survive on strong men but on strong institutions.” Weah described as a dangerous threat to democracy governments that claim to be democratic but are corrupt and collude with judges to undermine the rule of law and manipulate society. On his part, Rivers State Governor, Siminalayi Fubara, charged judges responsible for the administration of law and justice to consider the overall impact of their judgments on the polity. Fubara, who declared the conference open on Sunday, said law and order, as well as the rate of national development, were inextricably linked to the quality of justice courts deliver with integrity. He urged judges to ensure that nothing but the truth prevails at all times, irrespective of the status or social affiliations of the parties before them. “We cannot continue to insulate our laws from today’s reality; neither should justice remain shackled by unjust precedents, technicalities, inadequate access, undue delays, slavish adherence to rigid processes, political manipulation or brazen corruption. “The prevalence of these serious impediments to justice in our polity has damaged and continues to damage the reputation of the Judiciary and the Bar,” he said. Fubara said that in a democratic society, the legal system sets out the rules of conduct and provides the basis for the relationship between government, public and private institutions and citizens. Apart from upholding the rule of law, he said the judiciary was essential to any country seeking to foster true democracy, good governance and economic development. According to the governor, courts are not merely venues for resolving social disputes but serve as the ultimate refuge for all citizens, including the common man, to pursue justice, accountability, human dignity and the enforcement of their legal and constitutional rights. He said the ultimate aim of law was to protect and advance the security and well-being of citizens by ensuring equality before the law, safeguarding fundamental human rights and fostering an environment conducive to socioeconomic activities and national transformation. He noted that law, order, peace and meaningful progress prevail wherever the law is treated as sovereign, while denying the sanctity of the rule of law, true democracy and good governance negates the logic of civilised existence and constitutes a recipe for social disaster. “Consequently, we expect that our judges should not be mere apologists or conformists if they are to be the ultimate guardians of our democracy, the rule of law and the advancement of peace and good governance in our country,” he said. Fubara stated that public confidence in the quality of the nation’s judiciary would be enhanced only when judges demonstrate sound knowledge of the law, excellent legal reasoning, courage, commitment and integrity to hold the government and the governed equally accountable to the Constitution and the rule of law. “This is perhaps the only way to ensure that justice is not merely an ideal but one that can transform our society by being present in the life of our nation and of every citizen, including those at society’s margins, not just the privileged few. “It is said that in times of uncertainty, particularly when political power attempts to overreach the Constitution and the rule of law, it is the courage of the legal profession that can intervene to nip such aberrations in the bud and ensure that the exercise of power is not used to circumvent the laws of the land and the values of democracy,” he said. Addressing the theme of the conference, “Beyond Limits,” Fubara charged Nigerian lawyers, as ministers and custodians of the temple of justice, to rise above real or perceived constraints to protect the Constitution and advance the people’s inherent rights to democracy and good governance. “In Rivers State, we understand what it means to push beyond limits. We have walked through the furnace of power, may have been bruised, yet remain unbowed in our determination to safeguard our unity, peace and progress and are more resolved than ever in our commitment to delivering the dividends of democracy to our people,” he said. The post Weah calls for independent judiciary to safeguard democracy appeared first on Vanguard News .
